clue.text: Back to front objects without style

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside: the objects sit around the style

blocks.note: ends are aims or objects, as in 'ends and means'
a way of doing something is its style or manner

explanation.surface: A designer complains that some objects are back to front and lack any style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it is the older 'outside', so one word wraps the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Endways means with the end foremost, so something turned endways can be reversed in orientation.

clue.text: English manufacturing source needs frame to make material

indicators.note: a source is where something begins, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
the opening letter of manufacturing
the body is the frame or main structure

explanation.surface: An English textile mill needs a frame to produce cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like fabric for a mill, but here it means physical, as in giving a body to an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To embody an idea is to give it concrete physical form, which is making it material.

clue.text: Artists raised in gloomy environment create Venus de Milo look?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it upwards, so it reads from bottom to top
an environment surrounds whatever lives in it, so the word for gloomy wraps round the artists

blocks.note: dim means dark or gloomy
RAs are Royal Academicians, members of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: Artists in a dark studio set out to recreate the look of the Venus de Milo.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous ancient statue of Venus has lost both arms, hence the question mark on a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm, read literally, is to take away arms, which gives the armless appearance of that statue.

clue.text: Playing marimba's OK, Peter Pan-style

indicators.note: playing with things means toying with them, so these letters are moved about

blocks.note: taken as written, to be mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone's xylophone playing is fine, in a light whimsical style like Peter Pan.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Pan is famously pictured standing with hands on hips and elbows out.
explanation.definitionFit: The classic stance of Peter Pan in illustrations and pantomime is hands on hips, elbows pointing outward.

clue.text: Crush of people to see actor's bottom in dirty film

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter
'in' puts that single letter inside the word for the dirty film

blocks.note: scum is a dirty film on the surface of a liquid
the last letter of actor

explanation.surface: A crowd jostles to see an actor's backside in a smutty film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty film' suggests a seedy movie; it is the layer of grime on a pond or bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrum is a disorderly crowd pressing together, taken from the rugby formation.

clue.text: Very large opening for paint remover?

blocks.note: 'so' as in 'so good' means very
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A decorator asks whether a big opening is needed when using paint stripper.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as an example: a solvent is one kind of paint remover, not the only one.
explanation.definitionFit: Solvents such as white spirit dissolve dried paint, so a solvent is an example of a paint stripper.

clue.text: Woods in an unsettled area of Wales

indicators.note: unsettled things are disturbed and moved about, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be mixed up

explanation.surface: Forests in a wild, unpopulated part of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowdonia is the mountainous region and national park of north-west Wales around Snowdon.

clue.text: Latin name of tree belt

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Latin
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A botanist gives the Latin name of a tree belt, a strip of woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt' reads as a band of trees, but it is a verb, to strike hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To belt someone is to hit them hard, and to lash means to strike with a whip, a close synonym.

clue.text: Articulate rock band question tune's rendering

indicators.note: a rendering is a fresh performance or version, so these letters are played in a new order

blocks.note: ELO is the Electric Light Orchestra, a rock band
Q is the abbreviation for question
taken as written, to be mixed up with the question letter

explanation.surface: A rock band's take on the tune asks a question in articulate form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' could be a verb; here it is the adjective, fluent in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloquent describes someone fluent and persuasive in speaking, which is what articulate means as an adjective.

clue.text: Chinese possibly follow a direction

blocks.note: to take a road is to follow it
taken as written
a way is a direction, as in 'this way'

explanation.surface: A Chinese person might follow a set direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese' looks like a nationality; it is the British shorthand for a Chinese meal, a typical takeaway, which is food bought to eat at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese meal is a common example of a takeaway, food bought from a restaurant to eat elsewhere.

clue.text: Book some travelling sweep

indicators.note: things travelling are on the move, so these letters move out of their order

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for book
these four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reserve a place on a travelling sweep, as if booking a seat on a tour.
explanation.walkthrough: A besom is a broom made of twigs tied to a handle; as a verb it means to sweep with one.
explanation.definitionFit: Besom is used as a verb meaning to clean with a twig broom, which is a dictionary synonym for that action.

clue.text: Rhizome, flower tip as well, rejected by reserve

indicators.note: the tip of a word here is its far end, so only the closing letter of flower is used
something rejected is sent back, so the words 'as well' are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the final letter of flower
'too' means as well, also
stock is a supply held in reserve

explanation.surface: A gardener lists rhizome and the tip of a flower as items a nursery reserve turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' tempts as a plant or as a river; only its final letter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Rootstock is another name for a rhizome, the underground horizontal stem of a plant.

clue.text: Made do with iron arrangement for a traditional scalar structure

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be mixed up
taken as written, to be mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone improvised with an iron to rig up an old ladder-like framework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scalar' is about musical scales, not ladders or mathematics: a mode is a kind of scale.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dorian mode is one of the old church modes, a pattern of tones and semitones used as a musical scale.

clue.text: Cat gets over drugged state

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the word for drugged runs backwards

blocks.note: someone high on drugs is up
MA is the postal abbreviation for Massachusetts, a US state

explanation.surface: A cat recovers from a drugged stupor, perhaps after a trip to the vet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drugged state' reads as one phrase, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A puma is a large American wild cat, also called a cougar or mountain lion.

clue.text: One upgrade tentatively settled

indicators.note: done tentatively means tried out experimentally, so the letters are tried in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, to be mixed up

explanation.surface: A single upgrade has been provisionally decided on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tentatively settled' reads as one phrase, but 'tentatively' belongs to the wordplay alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something agreed upon has been decided by all parties, so it is a settled matter.

clue.text: Ulterior motive – as a solver might discern in stag (endangered)

blocks.note: a solver discerns a word concealed in the clue's letters, that is, one which is concealed
the word sitting across the end of stag and the start of endangered

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a secret purpose behind a stag night in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes itself: the solver finds AGENDA concealed in 'stAG ENDAngered', so the agenda is hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden agenda is a secret aim behind someone's actions, which is exactly an ulterior motive.

clue.text: 'Add vinegar etc to fish' : Jamie's ultimate restaurant rule?

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so only the closing letter of the name is kept

blocks.note: to dress a salad is to add vinegar, oil and so on
cod is a fish
the last letter of Jamie

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction quoted from celebrity chef Jamie Oliver, posing as his restaurant's rule.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks suggest a recipe; the question mark marks the definition as one example of where such a rule applies.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress code is a rule on what clothes are allowed, as many smart restaurants impose.

clue.text: In court, as ballet dancers often are

blocks.note: first meaning: a barrister practising law, or a defendant facing trial
second meaning: standing at the handrail used for ballet exercises

explanation.surface: Ballet dancers often end up in court, a playful slur on the profession.
explanation.walkthrough: A barre is the handrail ballet dancers train at; the answer spells it as the legal 'bar', whose sound matches.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means practising as a barrister or in the dock, and, by sound, at the handrail of a dance studio.

clue.text: What constitutes a list of arguments against storing canvas?

indicators.note: something storing another holds it inside, so one word is kept within the other

blocks.note: cons are arguments against, as in pros and cons
a tent is made of canvas

explanation.surface: Someone asks what really makes up a list of objections to keeping canvas in store.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs into 'of', which here only joins; the list is a book's or a box's table of what is inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A contents list sets out the items or chapters inside something, so contents are what such a list consists of.

clue.text: Agitator reduced temperature at Moscow mint?

blocks.note: temperature cut down to its abbreviation
the rouble is the Russian currency, so Moscow's coin
a mint is a maker of money

explanation.surface: An agitator lowers the temperature of a meeting held at the Moscow mint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moscow mint' reads as a place but splits into currency and the maker of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A troublemaker stirs up discord, which is what an agitator does.

clue.text: Bill Clinton famously claimed he didn't fit after being elected

definitions.text: Bill Clinton famously claimed he didn't

indicators.note: 'after' sends the word for fit to the second position, behind the word for elected

blocks.note: a candidate elected is in office
hale means healthy, fit

explanation.surface: Bill Clinton claimed he was not up to the job once he was voted in.
explanation.walkthrough: Clinton said in 1992 that he had tried marijuana but 'didn't inhale'. The fit piece comes after the elected one.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is a famous quotation in which Clinton denied taking smoke into his lungs, so the verb completes it.

clue.text: 100-year gravitational source linked to inverted star constellation

indicators.note: a source is where something begins, so only the opening letter of gravitational is kept
turned upside down in a down clue, so the word for star runs bottom to top

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
Y is the abbreviation for year
the opening letter of gravitational
the Sun is our star

explanation.surface: A sciencey sentence about a century-old gravity source tied to a constellation.
explanation.walkthrough: The astronomical surface makes 'star' look like part of the definition, but it supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cygnus, the Swan, is a northern constellation containing the bright star Deneb.

clue.text: African people incarcerated when borders removed

indicators.note: borders are the outer edges, so taking them away strips the first and last letters

blocks.note: to be shut up is to be locked away

explanation.surface: Members of an African people are jailed once frontiers are taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borders' suggests national frontiers in an African story; here it is the outside letters of a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hutu are an ethnic group of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

clue.text: Since start of Cup Final a 'new' heartless City's domination

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
with no heart means the middle of the word is taken away

blocks.note: 'as' can mean since, because
the opening letter of Cup
the end is the final part
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
the word itself, before its centre is removed

explanation.surface: A football report on a cup final where a new-look but spiritless City side dominated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup Final' looks like the football match, but it splits into two pieces. Dropping the middle two letters of City leaves its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendancy is a position of power or control over others, so it means domination.

clue.text: Debut made by crossword clue solver?

blocks.note: first meaning: a first appearance, an arrival
second meaning: the word a solver writes in the grid

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads as describing the solver's debut, but it is the thing a solver writes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a first coming in, such as a debut, and also a single answer filled into a crossword grid.

clue.text: Boost Chinese and UK measures of distance

blocks.note: a li is a Chinese unit of distance, about half a kilometre
FT abbreviates feet, imperial measures of length

explanation.surface: Someone boosts sales by using both Chinese and British units of length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese and UK measures' reads as one list, but each nation gives its own unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lift is an encouraging boost, as in a lift to morale.

clue.text: Marsupial as well as one canine housed in compartment

indicators.note: things housed in something are lodged inside it, so the first pieces go within the compartment

blocks.note: the boot is the luggage compartment of a car
'and' means as well as
the Roman numeral for one
C is the dentists' shorthand for a canine tooth

explanation.surface: A marsupial and a dog travel together, shut in a compartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' suggests a dog, but it is the tooth, which dental charts mark with C.
explanation.definitionFit: The bandicoot is a small Australian and New Guinean pouched mammal, so it is a marsupial.

clue.text: Hock about right with this?

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the word for hock goes round the letter for right

blocks.note: to hock something is to pawn it
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether hock is the right wine to drink with this dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Hock is a German white wine, a natural partner for shellfish, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole, the clue asks what hock suits: a prawn, a shellfish eaten with white wine.

clue.text: 'Eggs Placed Over Paving' gains show prize

indicators.note: something placed over another covers it, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: roe is the mass of eggs of a fish
a sett is a stone block used for paving a road

explanation.surface: A recipe titled 'Eggs Placed Over Paving' wins a prize at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make it look like a dish name, which is pure disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is the ribbon badge awarded to winners at shows such as horse or flower shows.

clue.text: New York suburbs crazy to change leader

definitions.note: plural phrase for a single place: Yonkers is one city in New York's suburbs

indicators.note: changing the leader means swapping the opening letter for another one

blocks.note: bonkers is informal for mad

explanation.surface: Somebody calls the New York suburbs mad enough to want new leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first letter is swapped; the clue does not say which letter replaces it, so the definition must decide.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonkers is a city just north of the Bronx, part of New York City's suburban fringe.
